claims.text: The initial material is an equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy with a homogeneous microstructure and no pre-existing silver-rich phases.
Introducing approximately 5 vol% silver by vacuum arc melting and homogenization will produce uniformly distributed silver-rich secondary phases in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Mechanical shear will cause the silver-rich secondary phases to migrate and coalesce at the sliding surface.
The surface-segregated silver will form an in-situ lubricious tribolayer.
The silver-containing tribolayer will be self-healing or self-repairing during sliding.
The ductile silver-rich film will provide a low-shear interface.
The silver-rich film will minimize direct asperity contact.
The silver-rich film will accommodate interfacial stress.
The dynamically formed film will repair micro-cracks.
Adding approximately 5 vol% silver will reduce the coefficient of friction by approximately 40% relative to identically processed, untreated CoCrFeMnNi.
Adding approximately 5 vol% silver will reduce wear rate by 30–50% relative to identically processed, untreated CoCrFeMnNi.
The predicted friction and wear improvements will be maintained from room temperature to approximately 400°C.
The predicted improvements will apply under both dry and boundary-lubricated sliding conditions.
Above approximately 400°C, phase instabilities or altered silver-segregation dynamics may diminish the tribological benefit.
Prior literature on silver-induced lubrication supports the proposed mechanism.
